claim: In the HWA laboratory, PRIO_TEST with LIMIT 2 showed: priority 0 stayed HOLD (never launched), numeric priorities 10/20/50 ran SUCC, and HI/GO ran SUCC and could run despite LIMIT. This matches documented limit/priority behavior.
supporting_quote: PRIO_00 HOLD; PRIO_10 SUCC; PRIO_20 SUCC; PRIO_50 SUCC; PRIO_HI SUCC; PRIO_GO SUCC.
notes: Priority 0 prevents launch; HI/GO bypass the workstation CPU limit; the stream showed STUCK with LIMIT 2 while jobs queued.

claim: In the HWA laboratory, with FENCE 20 on MDMDA, jobs of priority 10 and 20 entered the FENCE state and did not run, while jobs of priority 30, HI and GO ran SUCC. This confirms fence blocks jobs with priority less than or equal to the fence.
supporting_quote: FENCE_10 FENCE; FENCE_20 FENCE; FENCE_30 SUCC; FENCE_HI SUCC; FENCE_GO SUCC.
notes: FENCE was later reset to 0 after the test to restore the baseline.

claim: In the HWA laboratory, a folder LAB was created with composer mkfolder and navigated with chfolder; a job JOB_A was added inside it. composer replace updated JOB_A from lab_ls.sh/RECOVERY STOP to fail_continue.sh/RECOVERY CONTINUE, while composer modify failed in batch because it is interactive.
supporting_quote: composer replace returned AWSJCL003I update completed on jd=MDMDA#JOB_A; modify returned AWSBHW008E.
notes: Job definitions in a folder require the $jobs prefix in the definition file; modify is interactive while replace is the batch update command.
